submissions.title: San Francisco supervisor seeks moratorium on new data centers
submissions.excerpt: We don't know what impacts any of these data centers have, regardless of the footprint, regardless of the size
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: SF Supervisors Shamann Walton, Connie Chan, Jackie Fielder and Chyanne Chen introduced an urgency ordinance for a 45-day interim zoning moratorium on new data center land-use permits citywide, with a Board of Supervisors vote scheduled 2026-09-15. Requires a 4/5 vote; could be extended to roughly 22 months pending a Planning Commission impact study. Directly motivated by the NOVVA facility at 400 Paul Ave in Bayview (~36MW planned build-out, first ~9MW live since summer 2026) -- NOVVA is not currently a tracked project in this database, and no tracked project is sited in San Francisco. Reviewer may want to add NOVVA as a project so this restriction can attach explicitly per the siting-restriction rule (restrictions attach to projects, never inferred from location).

submissions.title: Data center moratorium sought by Oakland Councilmember Carroll Fife
submissions.excerpt: There need to be some protections, because we don't have any legislation on the books right now
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: Oakland Councilmember Carroll Fife introduced urgency legislation on 2026-09-11 for an immediate 45-day moratorium on land-use approvals and entitlements for new data centers citywide, alongside a planned permanent amendment to Oakland Planning Code Title 17; a hearing before the Life Enrichment Committee is set for 2026-09-22. Prompted largely by opposition to a proposed Behring Companies downtown AI facility, which Fife says is smaller than the 'mega-facility' residents fear. No tracked project in this database is sited in Oakland; the Behring proposal isn't yet tracked and may be worth adding once its scale/MW is confirmed.

submissions.title: Hayward Council to consider move to ban data centers at its Sept. 15 meeting
submissions.excerpt: directing staff to begin the process of amending the Hayward zoning code to prohibit development of new data centers
submissions.note: SITING RESTRICTION: Hayward Mayor Mark Salinas, Mayor Pro Tem George Syrop and Councilmember Angela Andrews referred a proposal to the City Council (vote scheduled 2026-09-15) directing staff to draft a zoning amendment that would ban new data center development citywide, plus a process to monitor/report impacts of data centers already approved or operating. Follows an April 2026 municipal code change requiring Major Conditional Use Permit approval (public hearing + Council vote) for any new data center application. No tracked project in this database is sited in Hayward; local coverage names the ~76.6MW STACK SVY03A facility as a driver of the backlash -- may be worth adding as a tracked project. Could not confirm the exact publication day of this city release in this research run (URL indicates August 2026; publicationDate left blank rather than guessed).

submissions.title: Egypt moves to build $1bn AI data centre with Nvidia tech
submissions.excerpt: aiming for a 200-megawatt facility worth $1 billion, using Nvidia technology
submissions.suggestedProjectName: Egypt Nvidia AI Data Centre (Vodafone / Elsewedy / Cassava)
submissions.note: NEW project candidate. Announced 2026-09-09 by Egypt's Minister of Communications & IT Raafat Hindi: a $1B, 200MW full-build target AI data center using Nvidia technology, built by a consortium of Vodafone Business, Elsewedy Electric and Cassava Technologies (Nvidia's African partner), framed partly as a US-vs-Huawei competition play in Africa. Initial phase reported separately as ~20MW/$200M over an initial three-year build -- record 200MW/$1B as the full-build target only, matching this tracker's convention for phased announcements, not near-term capacity. This is a government-minister announcement carried only by secondary press so far; no company (Nvidia/Vodafone/Elsewedy/Cassava) primary statement was found in this research run.

claims.methodology: Full-build target figure stated by government minister at announcement, via secondary press coverage
